summary: Quarterly review covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Arkwell is seeing steady growth in inference usage on chat endpoints; cost increase tied to peak-hour spikes and a couple of long-context jobs. Customer is evaluating Dedicated/reserved capacity vs staying hosted; security and VPC footprint are top requirements. Agreed to a pilot for Dedicated capacity + technical deep dive on private deployment requirements.
topics: Roadmap alignment and pilot next steps
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Tran (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood CSM), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Johnson (Arkwell), Carlos Rivera (Arkwell), Priya Singh (Arkwell), Ethan Cole (Arkwell)

[00:00] Sophie Tran: hey everybody, thanks for joining the qbr for Arkwell, appreciate you all making time. we'll run through usage, costs, recent reliability items, and then discuss pilots and next steps.
[00:12] Maya Johnson: thanks Sophie, yeah excited to get caught up. quick note - Ethan's here to speak to the infra details.
[00:20] Daniel Kim: I'll just pull up the dashboard while we talk, give the token breakdown. sorry if the share is a bit slow.
[00:28] Carlos Rivera: no worries. yeah we had a couple questions on the billing spike last month.
[00:33] Sophie Tran: yep first slide - usage overview. Arkwell monthly tokens increased about 34% quarter-over-quarter, mostly driven by chat usage and some long-context summarization jobs that started mid-June. there are a few long-running batches that look like they were using full context for archival summaries.
[00:52] Priya Singh: are those our nightly jobs? I thought we switched to the short-window summarizer.
[00:58] Ethan Cole: some of the archival pipelines were left on full context, engineer oversight. we put in a temp fix but want to do a more robust batching approach.
[01:10] Ravi Patel: to add, a tuning recommendation we made was using prefix KV caching to reduce repeated context; it's showing up in the recommendations but not fully implemented. note: transcript sometimes shows KV "cash" in the logs, ha.
[01:21] Maya Johnson: ha yes we saw that note, thanks. so cost wise, what was the main driver? token count or model size?
[01:29] Daniel Kim: the spike is mostly token count during peak hours — you get 2x tokens per session on high-concurrency windows. model selection also contributed: a handful of flows used a larger 70B model for step 1 instead of the 13B variant.
[01:42] Sophie Tran: yeah that's an ops pattern we see: default model is sometimes set to the bigger family for better quality, but cost jumps. we recommended an A/B rollout to smaller model variants for non-critical flows.
[01:55] Carlos Rivera: what about latency? our product team flagged some tail-latency issues during black friday test runs.
[02:03] Daniel Kim: our traces show 95th percentile latency rose to about 420ms for the chat endpoint during peak. normal is around 180-220ms. there were two transient infra events on 2026-07-18 related to autoscaler lag.
[02:18] Sophie Tran: to be clear, those were in Hosted region us-west-2 and we had short-lived queueing from a GPU pool scale-up. we offered a workaround: pin to Dedicated pool or enable burst capacity.
[02:30] Priya Singh: Dedicated seems attractive, but we need clarity on cost and SLA. can you share an apples-to-apples comparison?
[02:38] Sophie Tran: absolutely, we'll send a cost model; typically Dedicated has lower per-token cost at steady throughput and offers an SLA for latency/uptime. tradeoff is commitment and provisioning lead-time.
[02:50] Maya Johnson: security is also a requirement. for the Dedicated pilot, we need VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs for data residency.
[02:59] Ravi Patel: yes on the SE side we can map those requirements. our private deployment checklist includes VPC routing, customer KMS/HSM patterns, and RBAC sync - though sometimes transcription in notes muddles HSM as 'H-M-S', so small AI quirk.
[03:12] Ethan Cole: will this require significant infra changes on our side?
[03:16] Ravi Patel: depends on the mode. Dedicated hosted in your account requires fewer changes; private on-prem will require network routes and a few dependencies (NFS for model cache, container runtime). I'll put a clear list.
[03:28] Maya Johnson: great. one thing - we ran a security review earlier and asked about SOC2 scope and log retention. can you re-share the security pack?
[03:36] Daniel Kim: yes will share SOC2 binder and the recent audit notes. we also have a compliance whitepaper for regional data residency.
[03:45] Priya Singh: on roadmap alignment - we're planning to expand to a third use case this year (support summarization for legal docs). need to understand quality regressions if we switch models/quantize.
[03:56] Sophie Tran: good point. we recommend running a small eval set pre/post quantization; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles and run quality monitoring. we'll include sampling guidance.
[04:06] Maya Johnson: do you have any known regressions with the newer quantization yet?
[04:10] Ravi Patel: a few edge cases on named-entity recognition in legal text, we advise validation sets. we'll coordinate on eval prompts.
[04:18] Carlos Rivera: can we also get the per-route cost by model? the dashboard is a bit coarse.
[04:23] Daniel Kim: yes I'll export a token-level CSV with model, route, and time buckets. that should help identify the heavy hitters.
[04:29] Sophie Tran: ok summary so far - action items for Redwood: pricing, security docs, export, SE checklist; Arkwell to confirm pilot scope and priority use cases.
[04:38] Maya Johnson: sounds good. timeline - we want to kick the pilot next month. can we get a tech deep dive next week or the week after?
[04:46] Ravi Patel: I'm available next Thu and Fri, I'll send times.
[04:50] Priya Singh: next steps - final approval depends on our procurement team; also need legal to review data processing addendum.
[04:58] Sophie Tran: we'll loop in Legal and Procurement contacts in the follow-up email.
[05:03] Ethan Cole: one more question - do you support automatic fallback to smaller models during congestion?
[05:08] Sophie Tran: yes smart routing can fallback to compatible variants by policy; you can set rules for latency vs cost. it's in the console under route policies. sometimes the transcript prints it as 'route police' which is funny.
[05:18] Maya Johnson: okay great. any final questions?
[05:22] Carlos Rivera: none from platform.
[05:24] Priya Singh: none. thanks everyone.
[05:27] Sophie Tran: thanks all, we'll send the follow-ups by Friday. recap of next steps in the notes and action items — Sophie to send pricing, Daniel to export usage CSV, Ravi to send private deploy checklist, Maya to confirm pilot scope. meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription errors (product names and acronyms). References shared: pricing deck (link: redwood/pricing/arkwell-q3.pdf), SOC2 pack (link: redwood/security/soc2-2026.pdf), usage CSV (to be attached in follow-up).
